[[Category:Human rights]]
In law, '''human rights''' are rights a person is entitled to by the '''unique virtue of being human'''.<ref>{{#cite:Q3952}}</ref>

== Common categories ==

=== Bodily sovereignty ===

In general, a person has sovereignty over their body, and can therefore

* consent to or refuse medical treatments,
* choose to donate a part of their body ([[blood donation]] and [[organ donation]]) to another person
** after their death
** during their life (in case of medical necessity of another person, etc.)

Their '''bodily sovereignty''' is also entitled to legal protection from infraction by others, including

* intentional or accidental infraction by
** other people
** organisations
** the state
* harm from
** nature
** machines and other artificial constructions

=== Jurisdictional differences ===

Across [[jurisdiction]]s, the exact contents of '''legally-protected bodily sovereignty''' are different:

* In some jurisdictions (e.g, France), the right to [[abortion]] is part of legal bodily sovereignty, whereas in other jurisdictions it may be a [[crime]];
* In some jurisdictions (e.g, [[European Union]]), a person's bodily integrity is always legally protected, i.e., no individual or organisation, including the state, can legally intentionally inflict corporal damage to a person, whereas in other jurisdictions, [[corporal punishment]], including the [[death penalty]], may be legally sanctioned.
